topIssues.title: Invalid interop message recovery runbook
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Write and test a runbook for recovering a chain after an invalid interop message is detected and a reorg is triggered.

Testing has shown a number of systems which don't smoothly handle the large reorg caused by an invalid interop message. Since it's important that invalid messages are never accepted, requiring manual intervention is a reasonable "safety over liveness" policy. We need alerting in place to detect the situation and a clear runbook to follow in response.

topIssues.title: op-reth: interop tx pool does not resume after failsafe is disabled (requires restart)
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Summary

When the op-interop-filter failsafe is enabled and then disabled, **op-reth's transaction pool does not resume accepting interop (executing-message) transactions** until op-reth is restarted. The filter and `proxyd` recover within seconds, but op-reth stays in the failsafe-evicted state and silently drops interop txs (accepted by the RPC, never included; receipt lookup returns `not found`).

Observed on **interop-bench-3** with **op-reth `v2.2.6-rc.3`** on 2026-06-02.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Healthy two-chain interop devnet (executing messages land normally).
2. Enable failsafe on the op-interop-filter: `admin_setFailsafeEnabled true`.
3. Submit an executing message → correctly rejected (expected).
4. Disable failsafe: `admin_setFailsafeEnabled false`.
5. Submit executing messages → **still dropped for many minutes** (`not found` / never included), even though failsafe is off.

## Evidence that op-reth is the stuck component

- **Filter recovered:** `interop_checkAccessList([], "unsafe", …)` against the filter returns `null` (success), and a fabricated entry returns `failed to parse access entry` — i.e. the filter is healthy and actively validating, not in failsafe.
- **proxyd recovered (~10s):** chain B `proxyd-public` logs flip back to `interop access list validated successfully` within ~10s of disabling failsafe (it marks the filter backend unhealthy for `load_balancing_unhealthiness_timeout`, default 10s, then re-probes).
- **op-reth did NOT recover:** op-reth logged
  ```
  txpool::interop  failsafe enabled: evicting all interop transactions
  ```
  on activation and logged **no recovery**. Interop executing messages kept failing for >5 minutes after failsafe was cleared, while the filter and proxyd were both healthy. An independent `op-benchmark interop` re-check showed `0/1` executing messages succeeding post-toggle (vs `5/5` before any toggling).

So with the filter + proxyd healthy and failsafe off, op-reth's pool is the only layer still rejecting interop txs.

## Expected

After failsafe is disabled, op-reth should re-poll/re-validate and resume accepting interop transactions without operator intervention.

## Actual

op-reth's interop tx-pool stays evicted until the op-reth process is restarted:
```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/op-reth -n <chain-op-reth-namespace>
```

## Notes

- May be version-specific to `op-reth v2.2.6-rc.3`; please confirm against current builds.
- Documented in the op-interop-filter failsafe runbook (RB-336).

topIssues.title: EVM Engineering: standardized custom natspec
topIssues.author: smartcontracts

topIssues.author: smartcontracts

## Summary

- Adds a new **Releases** section under the Notices tab in docs.optimism.io
- Per-component release pages for 13 components across `ethereum-optimism/optimism` and `ethereum-optimism/infra`
- Mintlify `<Update>` components with date labels, stripped version numbers, and filter tags (Latest, Stable, Release Candidate)
- Overview index page with latest-per-component horizontal cards
- Network Notices index page (`notices/index.mdx`) with a maintenance comment keeping it in sync with `docs.json`
- `generate-releases.ts` prebuild script that fetches GitHub Releases API at build time — supports multiple repos, auto-detects RCs, guarantees the RC filter always renders on every page

## Components covered

**Protocol:** op-node, kona-node, op-batcher, op-proposer, op-challenger  
**Execution:** op-reth  
**Fault Proofs:** kona-client, kona-host  
**Contracts:** op-contracts  
**Tooling:** op-conductor, op-deployer, proxyd, op-acceptor

## Keeping it up to date

Re-run `pnpm prebuild` from `docs/public-docs/` to refresh. Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var to avoid the 60 req/hr anonymous rate limit. A Mintlify Workflow (weekly schedule) can be configured to keep pages current automatically — see the prompt in the PR description comments.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm prebuild` runs without errors
- [ ] `mintlify dev` shows Notices tab with Network Notices and Releases groups
- [ ] Each component page renders with intro text, filter tags, and Update entries
- [ ] Latest, Stable, and Release Candidate filters appear on every component page
- [ ] `/notices/upgrade-19` still resolves (no broken existing URLs)
- [ ] Index page shows horizontal Latest Releases cards and Info callout

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth/proofs): backfill the proofs window backward
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds the ability to extend an OP proofs storage window backward — taking a node that's been running with a recent earliest and rewriting older historical records so the window covers earlier blocks. This is the foundational implementation; the merge-walk-based compute is correct but per-block cost scales with proof-window depth. Optimizations will follow in separate PRs.

Three pieces:
- API trait OpProofsBackfillProvider — a prepend-style writer surface alongside the existing OpProofsProviderRw. Mirrors prune in reverse.
- V2 MDBX implementation(MdbxProofsProviderV2) — prepend_block(block_ref, diff) writes the four V2 changeset tables and front-inserts into the four history-bitmap tables, then moves earliest to the parent.
- BackfillJob — the driver. Iterates from current earliest down to target_earliest_block, computing each block's diff and calling prepend_block. Per-step state-root validation against the reth header.

**Tests**

- [x] Full crate suite (269 tests) passes locally.
- [x] V2 backend tests (db/store_v2/tests.rs) cover `prepend_block` tests
- [x] BackfillJob integration tests (backfill/tests.rs)
 
**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

Closes #20790
